title: Interim forecasts against the books
question: How far were the district's mid-year forecasts of its general-fund balance from what its books then showed?
finding: In March 2025 the district certified it might not meet its obligations (a negative certification) on a forecast that the general fund would end 2024-25 at $269.4 million; the unaudited books show $428.9 million, $159.5 million more (unrestricted part: $132.5 million forecast, $221.2 million actual). For 2025-26 the first interim forecast $215.1 million and the books show $301.8 million (+$86.7 million), although the adopted budget had put it higher, at $329.7 million. The unrestricted balance did fall, from $221.2 million to $83.5 million, mostly through a $111.5 million transfer the interim planned into the special reserve fund.
how: SACS Form 01 / 01I lines "Ending Balance, June 30 (E + F1e)": interim column "Projected Year Totals", unaudited column "Unaudited Actuals". Certification read from the ticked box on Form CI.
limits: Unaudited figures can change at audit. Interim forecasts must assume every budgeted cost is spent; unspent restricted grants, late State payments and vacancies raise year-end balances. A cautious forecast is required of districts in fiscal distress and is not misstatement. The 2025-26 second interim is not on disk.

rows.report: Adopted budget (as printed in the 2024-25 unaudited actuals)
